steps.message:
Reconstruct the running machine as a NixOS 26.05 VM. You have 60 minutes.

Start the reference with `/opt/runtime/reference start` and get a root shell
with `/opt/runtime/guest`. Forwarded ports (host→guest): 2222→22, 5353→53 (TCP and UDP), 8853→853. Its
configuration and behavior are the specification. Changes to it are disposable.

Graded: everything that affects how this machine is used by its clients,
users and operator. The goal is a drop-in replacement. Differences that come
only from the OS don't matter: kernel and version strings, package names, where system config files live, stock utilities nobody here is likely to need. Paths, names, identities, credentials, defaults and the commands people are likely to use for this machine's job do. No data migration: recreate what the server was
provisioned with (accounts, keys, seeded configuration data), not data its users
added later.

Submit /app/submission/replica.nix, a plain NixOS module, plus local supporting
files. A minimal module is supplied. The harness imports it against the pinned
nixpkgs 26.05 at /opt/nixpkgs (revision in /opt/contract/flake.lock) with
Nix 2.35.4 on x86_64-linux and system.stateVersion = "26.05". No flake or lock
file is needed; use the normal pkgs/lib/config arguments. The build has no
network access.

The harness provides boot resources, port forwarding, root SSH and TLS: the server
certificate and key are installed at /etc/node23/server.{crt,key}, and clients
trust /opt/contract/ca.crt.

Tools:
- `/opt/contract/check-replica [--syntax-only]` parses your Nix files and
  evaluates the full VM configuration without building or booting.
- `/opt/contract/build-replica` builds it. From a fresh writable directory, run
  /app/replica-vm/bin/run-*-vm. Candidate forwarded ports: 3222→22, 9353→53 (TCP and UDP), 9853→853; `GUEST_SSH_PORT=3222 /opt/runtime/guest` opens its root shell.

The verifier boots a fresh disk from your submission, connects with ordinary
clients, runs small programs as the existing users, and inspects effective
configuration. Passwords and fixture TLS keys on this lab machine are public.

Only /app/submission transfers to the verifier. Use real services. Do not copy
or embed the reference OS, fetch a remote answer, import paths outside your
submission and /opt/contract, or contact the reference at verification time.
I'll start by looking at the contract, the minimal module, and the reference machine.

    echo "Parsing $file" >&2
    nix-instantiate --parse "$file" >/dev/null
    COUNT=$((COUNT + 1))
done < <(find "$SUBMISSION" -type f -name '*.nix' -not -path '*/.git/*' -print0)

nix eval --json --option allow-import-from-derivation false "${EVAL_OPTIONS[@]}" \
    drvPath
echo 'Configuration evaluation passed. No build or VM boot was performed.' >&2

# /lib/systemd/system/dnsdist.service
[Unit]

Documentation=https://dnsdist.org
Wants=network-online.target
After=network-online.target

[Service]
ExecStartPre=/usr/bin/dnsdist --check-config
# Note: when editing the ExecStart command, keep --supervised and --disable-syslog

User=_dnsdist

Type=notify
Restart=on-failure
RestartSec=2

== nsd
# /lib/systemd/system/nsd.service
[Unit]
Description=Name Server Daemon
Documentation=man:nsd(8)
After=network.target

[Service]
Type=notify
Restart=always
ExecStart=/usr/sbin/nsd -d -P ""
ExecReload=+/bin/kill -HUP $MAINPID
# CAP_NET_ADMIN and CAP_NET_RAW required for IP_TRANSPARENT
CapabilityBoundingSet=CAP_CHOWN CAP_IPC_LOCK CAP_NET_BIND_SERVICE CAP_NET_ADMIN CAP_NET_RAW CAP_SETGID CAP_SETUID CAP_SYS_CHROOT

NoNewPrivileges=true
PrivateDevices=true
PrivateTmp=true
ProtectHome=true

ProtectKernelModules=true
ProtectKernelTunables=true
ProtectSystem=strict

RuntimeDirectory=nsd
RestrictRealtime=true
SystemCallArchitectures=native
SystemCallFilter=~@clock @cpu-emulation @debug @keyring @module @mount @obsolete @resources

[Install]

arguments.command:
G=/opt/runtime/guest; $G 'cat > /tmp/q.sh <<"EOF"
for q in "a23.test SOA" "a23.test NS" "a23.test MX" "a23.test TXT" "app1.a23.test A" "www.a23.test A" "_svc._tcp.a23.test SRV" "x.wild.a23.test A" "long.a23.test A" "big.a23.test TXT" "blocked.a23.test A" "a23.test ANY" "ext.a23.test A" "ns.i23.test A" "host1.i23.test A" "svc.n23.test A" "db.n23.test A" "example.com A" "nonexist.a23.test A" "11.2.0.192.in-addr.arpa PTR"; do set -- $q; echo "== $q"; dig +time=2 +tries=1 @127.0.0.1 -p 5353 $1 $2 2>&1 | grep -E "status|^[a-z0-9_.*-]+[[:space:]].*IN|flags:" | head -8; done
echo "== CHAOS"; dig +time=2 +tries=1 @127.0.0.1 -p 5353 version.bind CH TXT | grep -E "status|IN"
echo "== TCP big"; dig +tcp +time=2 +tries=1 @127.0.0.1 -p 5353 big.a23.test TXT | grep -E "status|flags|Query time" 
echo "== UDP big"; dig +bufsize=512 +time=2 +tries=1 @127.0.0.1 -p 5353 big.a23.test TXT | grep -E "status|flags|Query time"
echo "== DoT"; openssl s_client -connect 127.0.0.1:8853 -servername x 2>/dev/null </dev/null | head -3
EOF
bash /tmp/q.sh' 2>&1 | head -150
arguments.description: Run DNS query baseline against reference

steps.message: I queried the recursor directly on 5353 inside the guest, not dnsdist on 53, so these results bypass the policy rules. I'll repeat against port 53 and add the policy cases (ANY, CHAOS, sinkhole, rate limit, DoT).

arguments.command:
G=/opt/runtime/guest; $G 'cat > /tmp/q2.sh <<"EOF"
for q in "a23.test SOA" "a23.test MX" "blocked.a23.test A" "blocked.a23.test TXT" "sub.blocked.a23.test A" "a23.test ANY" "ext.a23.test A" "svc.n23.test A" "example.com A" "nonexist.a23.test A" "11.2.0.192.in-addr.arpa PTR" "ns.i23.test A"; do set -- $q; echo "== $q"; dig +time=2 +tries=1 @127.0.0.1 $1 $2 2>&1 | grep -E "status|IN" | head -4; done
echo "== CHAOS"; dig +time=2 +tries=1 @127.0.0.1 version.bind CH TXT | grep -E "status|IN"
echo "== TCP big"; dig +tcp +time=2 +tries=1 @127.0.0.1 big.a23.test TXT | grep -E "status|Query time|TC" 
echo "== UDP big"; dig +bufsize=512 +time=2 +tries=1 @127.0.0.1 big.a23.test TXT | grep -E "status|flags|Query time"
echo "== DoT"; timeout 5 openssl s_client -connect 127.0.0.1:853 -servername x </dev/null 2>/dev/null | grep -E "subject|issuer|Protocol|Cipher" | head -5
echo "== RL"; for i in $(seq 1 120); do dig +tries=1 +time=1 @127.0.0.1 a23.test SOA +short >/dev/null 2>&1; done; dig +time=2 +tries=1 @127.0.0.1 a23.test SOA +short; echo rc=$?
EOF
bash /tmp/q2.sh' 2>&1 | head -150
arguments.description: Run policy-aware DNS queries against dnsdist

steps.message: dnsdist 2.0 rejects the positional arguments to `webserver()`, which 1.6.1 accepted with a deprecation warning. I'll move those settings into `setWebserverConfig()`, which 1.6.1 also supports, so the behaviour is unchanged.

p='/app/submission/files/dnsdist.conf'

steps.message:
The build is still running. I've armed a monitor and will continue once the build finishes and I can test the VM.

Status so far:
- The NixOS module at `/app/submission/replica.nix` evaluates cleanly with `check-replica`.
- The dnsdist config passes the 2.0.7 binary's own check after I moved the webserver settings into `setWebserverConfig()`.
- The recursor YAML validates against the 5.4.6 binary.
- The VM build is in progress. Its first run was stale, so I restarted it against the current module.

Next steps once it finishes: boot the candidate VM, compare DNS answers, DoT, sudo rules, and rec_control against the reference, and fix any differences.

cat > /tmp/cmp.sh <<'EOF'
for q in "a23.test SOA" "a23.test NS" "a23.test MX" "a23.test TXT" "app1.a23.test A" "www.a23.test A" "_svc._tcp.a23.test SRV" "x.wild.a23.test A" "long.a23.test A" "blocked.a23.test A" "blocked.a23.test TXT" "sub.blocked.a23.test A" "a23.test ANY" "ext.a23.test A" "ns.i23.test A" "host1.i23.test A" "svc.n23.test A" "db.n23.test A" "example.com A" "nonexist.a23.test A" "11.2.0.192.in-addr.arpa PTR"; do set -- $q; echo "== $q"; dig +time=3 +tries=1 @127.0.0.1 $1 $2 2>&1 | grep -E "status:|^[^;].*IN" ; done
echo "== CHAOS"; dig +time=3 +tries=1 @127.0.0.1 version.bind CH TXT | grep -E "status:|IN"

EOF

steps.message:
The submission at `/app/submission/replica.nix` builds into a VM that matches the reference on everything I could test: DNS answers, DoT, sudo, and the `rec_control` commands. The build and the full evaluation both pass.

**Submission files**
- `replica.nix`: the module.
- `zones/`: `a23.test.zone`, `192.0.2.rev.zone`, `i23.test.zone`, copied byte-for-byte from the reference.
- `files/`: `dnsdist.conf` and `extrarecursorhosts`, also copied from the reference.

**What the module reproduces**
- **Identity:** hostname `node23`, domain `n23.test`, resolver `127.0.0.1`. The firewall is off, because the reference's ufw is inactive.
- **Accounts:** `birch` (uid 1301) and `cedar` (uid 1302), with locked passwords as in the reference. The service accounts `pdns` and `_dnsdist` use NixOS-allocated ids, since fixed ids collided.
- **sudo:** `birch` may run `rec_control get *` and `wipe-cache *` without a password. `cedar` may run `get *` only. `sudo`/`admin` groups get full root with a password, as in the reference.
- **sshd:** key-only; the root key matches the reference.
- **NSD** on 127.0.0.1:5301 serves `a23.test` and the reverse zone, with XFR to 198.51.100.7.
- **Recursor** on 127.0.0.1:5353 forwards `a23.test` and the reverse zone to NSD, serves `i23.test` as an auth zone, and exports the `svc`/`db.n23.test` hosts. Its web API is on 8082 with the reference's key. The legacy `60-legacy.conf.dpkg-old` is deliberately not loaded, since it would open the recursor to `0.0.0.0/0`.
- **dnsdist** on 0.0.0.0:53 and 853 (DoT) with the reference's rules: ANY and CHAOS refused, the `blocked.a23.test` sinkhole, and the per-IP rate limit. The web API is on 127.0.0.1:8083.

**Choices and deviations**
- dnsdist is 2.0.7 in this nixpkgs, not 1.6.1. Its `webserver()` no longer takes positional arguments, so I moved those into `setWebserverConfig()`, which 1.6.1 also accepts.
- The recursor is 5.4.6, configured through its YAML schema. Its key names differ from the reference's 4.6 config, so I mapped each setting to its 5.x equivalent and checked the result with the binary.
- The harness installs `server.key` as root-only (0600), which would stop dnsdist from reading it for DoT. I widened it to `root:_dnsdist 0640`, which matches the reference.
- I installed `pdns-recursor`, `dnsdist`, and `bind.dnsutils` (dig, host, nslookup, nsupdate) system-wide. `rec_control` must be on the system PATH for the sudo rules to resolve.
- `/etc/resolv.conf` shows `domain` rather than `search`, and adds an `::1` nameserver, because NixOS's resolvconf adds them. Lookups behave the same.
- Not reproduced: `/opt/cinc` (a Chef client install with no config in the reference), snapd/lxd, cloud-init, and unattended-upgrades. None looks like part of this box's DNS job.

**Verification**
- `build-replica` succeeds with the final module, and the candidate boots.
- Against the reference, the DNS answers match on all 21 names I queried, including the policy cases, TCP fallback, and the CHAOS and ANY refusals. The only diffs are cache-timing TTLs and timestamps.
- DoT works from the host on the forwarded port with the lab CA, on TLS 1.3 and 1.2.
- Birch's `get` and `wipe-cache` and cedar's `get` run without a password; `get-all` and cedar's `wipe-cache` are refused, as the rules require.
- I did not test DoT from inside the candidate, because it has no `openssl`; the host test covers it.
